title: upgrade: attention kernels -> FlashAttnV2 with fused rotary/rope + KV batching & scheduling improvements
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Backwards-compatible performance upgrade: replace legacy attention kernels with FlashAttentionV2 variants, enable fused-rotary/rope code paths, and introduce better KV-cache-aware continuous batching and per-queue scheduling heuristics. Expected throughput and p95 latency improvements for long-sequence inference on NVIDIA GPUs.
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost and P95 latency regressions observed for long-context generations and streaming workloads. This PR upgrades our attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 variants, adds fused rotary/rope execution paths, and tightens integration with KV-cache and continuous-batching/scheduling logic. The goal is to be fully backwards-compatible at the API level while providing substantial runtime improvements for LLM serving. Changes: 1) Integrate FlashAttnV2 kernel selection path with runtime kernel registry; 2) Implement fused rotary/rope operators to avoid multiple memory passes for rotary/rope embedding transforms; 3) Introduce a KV-cache-aware batcher that groups requests by KV-shape and prefix-match probability to avoid unnecessary KV copy/concats; 4) Add per-GPU scheduling heuristic that prefers low-latency slots for interactive traffic and high-throughput slots for bulk generation; 5) Update model profiles and tuning parameters in the model-registry. Testing & validation: microbenchmarks for short/long sequences, end-to-end canary on dedicated pool, automated evals against quality regression prompts, and stress tests on continuous-batching scenarios. Rollout: staged canary by model (gpt-like 13B -> 70B) and by capacity tier; automatic fallback to legacy kernels on rare GPU-only kernel failures. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes; model artifacts unchanged. Related: ENG-4982 (kernels roadmap), ENG-5010 (batching scheduler), SUP-1122 (customer incident referencing p95 regressions).

review_comments: Miguel Rivera: Nice work. Two questions: 1) how do you handle mixed rotary/rope models at runtime? 2) any fallbacks for GPUs that don't have the new kernels?

Author (Asha Patel): We detect model config rotary vs rope at load time and set the fused path if available. For GPUs that don't have the optimized kernels we fall back to the legacy attention implementation; selection is dynamic and runtime logs surface the active kernel.
Priya Sharma: The KV-aware batcher looks promising. Can we add metrics for 'kv_shape_group' and 'prefix_match_rate' to the per-route dashboard?
Author (Asha Patel): Added metrics to the canary dashboard and the runtime emits kv_group and prefix_match tags; included in the PR's tests and the perf job.
Ethan Liu: CI failed once on Windows build matrix due to missing CUDA_TOOLKIT path; looks fixed in the follow-up commit. Approving after green CI.
Miguel Rivera: Approve after canary results look stable for 48h.
ci_checks: perf-regression-job: pass (no regression vs baseline on p95 and throughput)
benchmark_summary: A10 GPU (gpt-13b): throughput +28% for long-sequences (8k tokens), p95 latency -18%
A10 GPU (gpt-70b): throughput +15% for mixed short/long workloads, p95 latency -12%
Small-sequence (<=512): negligible change (+1-2%), no quality regression observed
End-to-end cost estimate: up to 22% token-cost reduction for typical streaming-heavy workloads due to KV reuse and fused ops
notes: Rollout plan: staged by model family, 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h windows with automatic rollback on kernel exceptions
Fallbacks: legacy kernels remain available and are selected when flashattn_v2 reports CUDA errors or OOMs
Monitoring: added kv_group, prefix_match_rate, kernel_active tags to runtime metrics; dashboards updated in canary
Documentation: perf_tuning.md updated with recommended settings and caveats for mixed rotary/rope models
